title: Teeth, false teeth and trumpet players
summary: Metoyer stressed caring for teeth. The men discuss trumpeters with false teeth, including Bunk Johnson and Gilbert Young, and Young's jitney work.

story.theme_name: The reed and horn player's craft: clarinet, sax, tone
story.community_name: Lips, teeth and breath: the physical craft of brass playing

blocks.x: Did he say anything about your teeth? Did he think that your teeth were important?

Well, yeah, let you take good care of your teeth, you see. And one thing he knows is, you know, if they're not projecting out in a way like that, that kind of, you know, way hurts you. If you're in a way that projecting teeth, they couldn't make no good trumpet players.

I guess most trumpet players think of their teeth as a friend of mine, a young white trumpet player, Jerry Blumberg, staying here in town for about a week. I offered him some candy on Easter, some Easter eggs. He said, no, he's a trumpet player. He won't eat any candy. He thinks about his teeth. He's crazy. Yeah. Played to eat candy.
It's a good thing to think about it, right?
It might affect, yeah, I guess. Did you ever know any trumpet players much with the false teeth that played? I know Bunk Johnson finally played with false teeth.
Well, Bunk Johnson had false teeth. Gilbert Young has false teeth.

Yeah. And he plays good. He'd take them out and play. He'd take them out and play without a team. He'd have none precious system about this world. He'd take them out. He'd have false teeth. And old man Lewis the man had quite a few false teeth. You know Gilbert Youngkin though?

When you had, before you got them false teeth, Gilbert Youngkin playing the side, either side or the middle. He had all these games. He'd get tired. He'd play. You ever get tired there, he'd play. I'm with you all over his mouth. Yeah, I was seeing him get his lip all bust up and he said, well, who's stopping him from playing?

He said, I've got more lip. He was another one of those jitney men. You know, he'd been there. He was on the jitney a long time with Earl Foster too. Right over there on the canal at the Alamo. Yeah, that was before Alvin Alcorn went in there. He went and got young this day.
